newsitem.title: UK: Intl CableTel plays down talk of UK DTT legal move.
newsitem.headline: Intl CableTel plays down talk of UK DTT legal move.

text.p: International CableTel said on Monday it was "premature" to talk of a legal challenge to a rival UK digital terrestrial television consortium comprising Carlton, BSkyB and Granada.
"We received details of their application only last week and we are not going through it in detail. We are still at the stage of evaluating the situation," an International CableTel spokeswoman said.
A report in the Independent on Sunday said International CableTel was set to launch a legal challenge to its rivals before the European Commission.
It said the company's lawyers planned to cite articles 85 and 86 of the Treaty of Rome, which prohibit restrictive trading and abuses of dominant market positions.
Carlton, BSkyB and Granada have formed the British Digital Broadcasting (BDB) consortium to apply for licences to operate new digital terrestrial television licences.
International CableTel is the only other applicant for the three network licences which can carry some 15 channels.

But BDB, linking Britain's leading pay television company with two major ITV companies, is regarded by analysts as the likely victor when the Independent Television Commission (ITC) awards the licences later this year.
